title: The last open range is checked up to ten times its start or $10,000
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin whose role has 'Settings — Parts' and 'See Financial Data'.
  • Have a new tier for this test, tier A, with a name no other tier uses.
  • Have a new matrix for this test, matrix A, pricing a new category made for this test, with two ranges, $0.00 to $1,000.00 and from $1,000.01: Default on + $ 2000 in both, tier A on % Off 10 in both.
  • Have a new matrix for this test, matrix B, pricing a new category made for this test, with two ranges, $0.00 to $5,000.00 and from $5,000.01: Default on + $ 2000 in both, tier A on % Off 10 in both.
  • Use a desktop browser window at least 1440 pixels wide, at 100% zoom, so every column of the page shows.
custom_steps:
1. Click the Matrices tab on Settings › Pricing.
  2. Click matrix A's name on the Matrices list.
  3. Click the Matrices tab on Settings › Pricing.
  4. Click matrix B's name on the Matrices list.
  5. Point at the warning icon beside tier A's last-range value.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Matrix A is listed.

Step 2:

  • Tier A's values in matrix A show no warning icon: the last range is checked up to $10,000.10 ($1,000.01 × 10 = $10,000.10), while tier A first sells below cost at $18,000.06 (0.90 × (cost + $2,000) falls below the cost above $18,000).
  • Tier A's values still show "10% off" in both ranges.

Step 3:

  • Matrix A is listed with matrix B.

Step 4:

  • In matrix B a warning icon shows beside tier A's last-range value: that range is checked up to $50,000.10 ($5,000.01 × 10 = $50,000.10).
  • Tier A's first-range value in matrix B has no warning icon (every cost up to $5,000 sells above cost).

Step 5:

  • A tooltip reads tier A's name followed by "sells a $18,000.06 part below cost." ($18,000.06 + $2,000.00 = $20,000.06, 10% off = $18,000.054, rounded to $18,000.05, below $18,000.06; at $18,000.05 the price rounds to $18,000.05, equal to the cost).
